evidence.section: The Age of Glory and Pride
evidence.claim: Official Dwarf construction includes walls. The passage describes specific works; their builders, age, locations and history are not assigned to a generated DF wall.

evidence.quote: Most Dwarf words have several meanings.
evidence.claim: Use explicitly selected colour and appearance senses. Combining those words into wall labels is a Forthammer composition, not a claim about an official wall-naming grammar.

evidence.quote: Bar A fortified gateway or door
evidence.claim: Bar supplies a protective gate image; bryn selects the shiny/brilliant sense. Neither asserts that the named wall contains a gate or precious metal.
Gorl is used in its colour sense, not its gold sense.

evidence.section: Khazalid Glossary / Klad, Kol, Mingol, Skarrenruf
evidence.claim: Klad, mingol and bar supply protective images. Kol and skarrenruf supply the black and bright-blue senses. Mingol retains its specific lowland-watchtower meaning; it is not translated as wall.
Only the red-colour sense is selected; no battle, wound or blood sacrifice is invented.

evidence.quote: stacked stone walls or dug out gun pits
evidence.claim: The army book corroborates wall-building and defensive engineering. No generated label certifies a Master Engineer, stone construction, successful defence or invulnerability.
Zan Mingol is an existing named location and is reserved, including joined and hyphenated forms through normalized filtering.

evidence.section: p.44, Khazalid Glossary: Duraz, Azul and Dok
evidence.quote: Dok Watch, observe, see, the eye
evidence.claim: Dok selects the eye as a vigilance image. Duraz and Azul on the same page supply stone and metal as image materials, never wall specifications or a claim of watch personnel.

evidence.quote: Galaz Gold of particular ornamental value
evidence.claim: Ornamental gold can qualify an eye, gate, tower or armour image without claiming a gold-built wall, treasure, invulnerability or prosperity.

evidence.section: p.47, Khazalid Glossary: Und and Wutroth
evidence.quote: Und A watchpost carved into the mountain-side
evidence.claim: Und supplies a specifically mountainside-watchpost image; it is not a generic word for wall or tower. Wutroth preserves wood from ancient mountain oak as the material of gate/tower imagery, not the wall or local landscape.

evidence.section: Of Karak Azgaraz / Unzaled Sky-Bridge and Migdhal Skarrenruf; Loremaster offset 232730
evidence.claim: The named guarded entry gives cultural context for vigilance imagery. Applying an eye or watchpost image to a wall is a new symbolic composition, not a claim about that canonical gateway or actual surveillance.

evidence.quote: Foremost among these is the Durazklad clan
evidence.claim: Durazklad is the canonical Stone Armour clan associated with Thorgrim Grudgebearer, not a free new compound. Exclude and reserve it instead of granting that identity or its founding story to a wall.
Silver and bread are attested independent concepts, not invented product or wealth claims.
The glossary distinguishes a musical horn from horn material, and attests road and thunder. Selected nouns remain literal word senses inside adapted labels.
The selected moonlight sense and the printed material, shadow, work and sunrise nouns add distinct concepts. No generic machine, dawn-direction, geology or ancestry meaning is invented.

The conjunction explicitly pairs two reviewed images. Thrag means wound, Thrynaz includes laws, Tiwaz includes rest and Skaud includes song. These are not new translations for hospital, government or tavern.

High-resolution printed text confirms Zunthrum with n. Spear, money, sunset, remembering and gift are independently attested; none assigns actual stock, wealth, a historical event or a commemorated person.
